description: Labeled cases for temporal_check.py: future-dated bibliography entries, fetched_at timestamps that predate their own publication year, and evidence cards that attribute a later year's development to an earlier source. Every case pins `today`, so the set measures the checker rather than the calendar. Negatives outnumber positives and are all near-misses — the boundary year, the uncorroborated source, the missing field — because those are the shapes a date checker fires on wrongly.

cases.comment: The realistic origin of this defect: 2027 typed for 2017, not a preprint from the future.

cases.comment: NEGATIVE. The boundary. A paper published this year is the ordinary case and must never fire.
NEGATIVE. fetched_at inside the publication year is normal; only fetching BEFORE publication is impossible.
NEGATIVE. The +1 boundary. Online-first in one year, issue-assigned the next, is routine — the checker only fires above a one-year gap.

cases.comment: NEGATIVE. A 2020 paper citing 1998 data is scholarship working normally, not an anachronism. The check is directional and must stay that way.

cases.comment: NEGATIVE. Without a recorded year there is nothing to compare against; guessing one would be exactly the fabrication the kit forbids.
NEGATIVE. A registry row with year 'in press' or null must be skipped, not coerced.
NEGATIVE. A missing year is bib_doctor's finding, not this checker's — two lints reporting the same defect teaches the author nothing twice.
NEGATIVE. A fetched_at that will not parse is a schema defect, deliberately left to bib_doctor rather than reported here as a temporal impossibility.
NEGATIVE. An empty project must report nothing rather than crash — the state every project is in on day one.

NEGATIVE. 2048 is ResNet-50's Global Average Pooling width — the only power of two inside the retained 20xx range and the most common feature dimension in computer vision. A DL review meets it in almost every extraction card.

cards.detail: the GAP layer gives 2048 features per image

cases.comment: NEGATIVE. A card may name ANOTHER study. 'Polater & Isik 2024' inside a card whose own source is from 2021 is a cross-reference, not a claim the 2021 paper made about 2024.

cards.detail: This mirrors Polater & Isik 2024, the same APTOS source

cases.comment: POSITIVE. The context guard must not blind the check to a real temporal claim: a 2019 source cannot report a 2024 revision.

mutations.breaks: The one-year tolerance disappears, so ordinary online-first-then-issue timing is reported as an anachronism.
The impossible direction is reversed, so a normal fetch is flagged and the real defect passes.

The context guard stops being consulted in the card loop, so a tensor dimension ('2048 features') and an author-year cross-reference are both reported as anachronistic citations. The helper staying correct while nothing calls it is the failure this mutation exists to catch.

Any capitalised word before a year counts as an author surname, so 'The 2022 recalibration protocol' is exempted as a citation and a genuine anachronism goes unreported. An exemption that swallows true positives is the same defect as the false positive it removed, reversed.
